messages:
Will: Heads-up — saw a ~18% drop in prefix cache hit-rate for model:gpt-small on prod after the opt-kernel-v3 rollout. dashboard -> https://redwood.app/dash/abc123 :eyes:
Cheng: saw the alert, thanks. initial glance at kernel-selection logs shows different code-paths for short contexts (<=64) now preferring fused-attn-k3. could be alignment with our keying scheme.
Tara: is the drop across all routes or concentrated?
Will: concentrated on /chat-stream and /summarize routes (99% of token saved regression). per-customer slice shows 3 tenants hit hardest.
Maddy: can you paste the profiler snippet? also any changes to batching heuristics recently?
Will: pasted pprof sample below from the 10:15 incident window:
```
(pprof) top 20
Total: 12.4s
  3.8s  30.6% runtime.memmove
  2.9s  23.4% kv_cache.Lookup
  1.6s  12.9% fused_attn_k3.forward
  1.2s   9.7% batching.Dispatch
  0.9s   7.3% model.RunStep
```
Will: note kv_cache.Lookup is higher than usual (normally ~1.1s).
Cheng: interesting — memmove spike probably from different tensor packing layout used by fused-attn-k3. if the kernel expects word-aligned blocks we might be shifting buffers which changes the prefix key bytes.
Tara: so key bytes differ, leading to lower reuse/higher miss? can that cause warmup to fail?
Cheng: yes, if the cache key includes raw pretokenized prefix bytes or offsets that change with kernel packing. our key normalizer currently only canonicalizes token sequences, not kernel-aligned shapes.
Maddy: we pushed batching tweaks last week (adaptive-window size lowered to 8 to reduce latency). that might change sequence padding and upstream key derivation.
Will: correlating events: batching tweak deploy @ 09:40, kernel switch @ 10:00, hit-rate drop @ ~10:12. combo likely.
perf-bot: Alert triggered: prefix-cache-hitrate drop (model:gpt-small) | delta -18% | token-saved loss ~420k tokens/hr.
Tara: can we get diffs of the raw keys for hits vs misses for a sample tenant? need minimal repro.
Will: grabbing 1k request sample now. will redact customer ids.
Cheng: also add kernel-selection metadata to the cache key audit log (kernel_name, packing_layout) — if we can correlate keys with kernel used we can confirm.
Maddy: quick mitigation idea: roll back kernel selection for short contexts to previous kernel (opt-kernel-v2) for the affected pool and re-run warmup. that should restore alignment while we fix normalizer.
Tara: agree. also add a metric: key-entropy-per-route so we can detect fragmentation early.
Will: rollback scheduled at 11:05 if no objections. ops-bot, can you coord?
ops-bot: @Will rollback job queued: job-id rdo-3221, expected 3m to finish. Will be posted to #eng-releases when done.
Cheng: follow-up items:
- add kernel metadata to cache key audit logs (short term)
- update key normalizer to canonicalize on token-level + padding-agnostic hash (mid term)
- add key-entropy-per-route and per-tenant drift alert (obs)
- run warmup backfill after rollback for affected tenants (ops)
Maddy: also check warmup sampler: our current warmup only uses top-k prefixes, but if kernel packing changed alignment we need to include padded variants as synthetic seeds.
Tara: logging note: please include sample base64 raw-key for misses (no PII) so we can diff.
Will: uploaded sample diff -> https://uploads.redwood/app/xyz (redacted). initial diff shows systematic byte shifts at 16-byte boundaries.
Cheng: that aligns with AVX-block packing in fused-attn-k3. padding introduced extra zeros leading to different serialized prefix bytes.
Will: action — rollback started. will update when hit-rate recovers.
(10:58) Will: rollback complete. perf-bot reports partial recovery in 2m.
perf-bot: Recovery: prefix-cache-hitrate delta now -3% (from -18%), token-saved loss reduced to ~60k tokens/hr.
Tara: good. keep the kernel change gated until normalizer + padding-agnostic hashing shipped.
Maddy: I'll open a PR for the normalizer with tests covering padded variants.
Cheng: I'll add kernel metadata to audit logs and a probe that logs key bytes + kernel used for a 0.1% sampling.
Will: Thanks all. follow-ups tracked in the ticket: INT-4823.
Maddy: tagging owners: @Cheng (kernel audit), @Maddy (normalizer), @Tara (observability)
Cheng: will post a short writeup on kernel-affinity vs cache-keying after we have the sample diffs.
Will: closing thread, moving discussion to INT-4823 and #eng-runtime for async updates. :thumbsup:
